2. When does a static variable get memory and how is it initialized?
A static variable gets memory in the
When the class loader completes its task, the JVM provides memory for the static variables.
The static variable is initially assigned its default value by the JVM.
Therefore, static variables belong to the class-level memory area rather than being created separately for every object.
3. When is a static block executed?
A static block is executed before the
After the JVM receives control back from the class loader, it checks for static elements. Static variables are initialized first, and the static block is executed before the

4. How can a static method be called?
A static method can be called using the class name without creating an object.
An object is not mandatory to call a static method.
This is one of the important differences between static and instance methods.
5. What is the simple-interest example used to understand static variables?
Consider a banking application where businessmen take loans.
Suppose a bank has many businessmen as customers.
The principal amount can be different for every businessman.
The loan period can also be different for every businessman.
However, if the bank's rate of interest is common to all businessmen, there is no need to create a separate copy of the rate for every object.
This situation demonstrates the purpose of a static variable.
6. Why should the rate of interest be made static in the banking example?
If the rate is an instance variable, every object receives its own copy.
Instead, one shared copy can be maintained using static.
Now all objects of the class can use the same static variable.
When one variable should be common to all objects of a class, make that variable static.
7. What is the difference between a static variable and an instance variable in the banking example?
P, T, and SI represent information that can differ for each businessman.
R represents the rate of interest, which is common to all businessmen.
The static variable has one shared copy for the objects of the class.

A method can be considered static when it can be called without creating an object.

28. What happens when a program contains multiple classes with static blocks?
A class is not simply loaded and initialized merely because it exists somewhere in the code.
When a particular class is accessed, that class can be loaded and its static initialization takes place.
Therefore, if a program contains multiple classes, it is important to determine:
When its constructor or other code executes.
The execution order must be traced from actual class access rather than assuming that every class is initialized immediately.
29. When is a class loaded during execution?
The execution discussed establishes that a class is loaded when it is accessed.
For example, if the first executable statement accesses a particular class, that class is loaded at that point.
A class that has not yet been accessed is not assumed to have already been loaded and initialized merely because it appears elsewhere in the code.
Therefore, while solving output questions involving static blocks and multiple classes, always identify the point at which each class is accessed.
30. What is the execution order involving a static block and a
When an object of a class is created, static initialization occurs before instance-level object initialization.
Therefore, when tracing a program containing a static block and constructor, the static block executes before the constructor for that class.
The exact overall output still depends on which class is accessed and at what point in the program.
